children.name: Artamus
children.description: The woodswallows — a genus of highly social, aerial insectivores with a superficial resemblance to swallows, for which they are named. They have broad, triangular wings, short tails, and stout, finch-like bills adapted for catching insects on the wing. They are among the most gregarious of all Australasian passerines, often packing tightly together on exposed branches in large, noisy flocks.

children.name: Artamus cyanopterus
children.description: The dusky woodswallow (Artamus cyanopterus) The global population of the species has as yet not been formally confirmed, but it has been officially rated in the range of 'Least Concern', according to the BirdLife International in 2004.

children.name: Artamus flaviventer
children.description: A woodswallow with yellow vent from the Moluccas and New Guinea.

children.name: Artamus fuscus
children.description: The ashy woodswallow, sometimes also called the ashy swallow-shrike, is a woodswallow which is found in south Asia. Like other woodswallows, it has a short curved bill, a short square tail and long wings. It is usually seen perched in groups, high on powerlines, tall bare trees and most often in areas with a predominance of tall palm trees.

children.name: Artamus leucoryn
children.description: The white-breasted woodswallow is a medium-sized passerine bird which breeds from the Andaman Islands east through Indonesia and northern Australia. The name "woodswallow" is a misnomer as they are not closely related to true swallows. Instead, they belong to the family Artamidae, which also includes butcherbirds, currawongs and the Australian magpie.

children.name: Artamus maximus
children.description: The great woodswallow (Artamus maximus), also known as the greater woodswallow, giant woodswallow or New Guinea woodswallow, is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Artamus melanops
children.description: A woodswallow with black face from the Lesser Sunda Islands.

children.name: Artamus mentalis
children.description: The Fiji woodswallow is a species of woodswallow in the family Artamidae. It is endemic to most of the islands of Fiji, although it is absent from Kadavu Archipelago and the Lau Archipelago. The species was once considered a race of the white-breasted woodswallow, which breeds from Australia, New Caledonia and Vanuatu through to Borneo and the Philippines.

children.name: Artamus minor
children.description: The little woodswallow (Artamus minor), is a bird patchily distributed over much of mainland Australia, avoiding only the driest deserts and the area within about 300 kilometres of the southern coastline, and showing a preference for rugged terrain around inland ranges.

children.name: Artamus personatus
children.description: Masked woodswallow (Artamus personatus) is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus
children.description: The butcherbirds — a genus of medium-sized, stocky passerines with strongly hooked bills bearing a distinct tooth-like notch, an adaptation for their predatory feeding habits. They earned their common name from their habit of impaling prey on thorns or wedging it in tree forks as a 'larder'. They are accomplished songsters with rich, flute-like calls.

children.name: Cracticus nigrogularis
children.description: The pied butcherbird (Cracticus nigrogularis) is a songbird native to Australia.

children.name: Cracticus torquatus
children.description: The grey butcherbird (Cracticus torquatus) is a widely distributed species endemic to Australia.

children.name: Cracticus quoyi
children.description: The black butcherbird (Melloria quoyi) is a species of butcherbird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus cassicus
children.description: The hooded butcherbird (Cracticus cassicus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Cracticus louisiadensis
children.description: The Tagula butcherbird (Cracticus louisiadensis) is a species of bird in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Gymnorhina
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Australian Magpie, one of Australia's most iconic and familiar birds. Despite its name, it is not closely related to the Northern Hemisphere magpies but belongs to the butcherbird family. It is a large, boldly patterned black-and-white bird with a famously complex and melodious carolling song, and is renowned for its territorial swooping during breeding season.

children.name: Gymnorhina tibicen
children.description: thumb|Adult with juvenile [[Taveuni, Fiji]].

children.name: Melloria
children.description: Melloria — a genus of woodswallows & butcherbirds in the family Artamidae.

children.name: Melloria quoyi
children.description: The black butcherbird is a species of butcherbird in the family Artamidae. It is found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
